added.title: Director of Advanced Technology Lab (ATL) Wafer Fabrication
added.description:
RELOCATION ASSISTANCE: Relocation assistance may be available

CLEARANCE REQUIRED FOR START: No

CLEARANCE TYPE: SCI

TRAVEL: Yes, 10% of the Time

Description

At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. Our pioneering and inventive spirit has enabled us to be at the forefront of many technological advancements in our nation's history - from the first flight across the Atlantic Ocean, to stealth bombers, to landing on the moon. We look for people who have bold new ideas, courage and a pioneering spirit to join forces to invent the future, and have fun along the way. Our culture thrives on intellectual curiosity, cognitive diversity and bringing your whole self to work — and we have an insatiable drive to do what others think is impossible. Our employees are not only part of history, they're making history.

Northrop Grumman Mission Systems is seeking an experienced and strategic Director of Advanced Technology Lab (ATL) Wafer Fabrication
to lead a critical semiconductor manufacturing organization at our Linthicum, Maryland facility. This leader will oversee wafer fabrication operations and engineering in support of both production and advanced technology development. This is a significant leadership opportunity within a unique, defense-focused semiconductor manufacturing environment. The Director will play a central role in strengthening operational execution, advancing manufacturing performance, and aligning engineering and operations to support mission-critical program and business priorities.

About Advanced Technology Lab (ATL)

Advanced Technology Lab (ATL), located outside of Baltimore, Maryland, designs, manufactures, and tests semiconductor products supporting internal and commercial production customers as well as emerging technology programs. Northrop Grumman’s ATL semiconductor foundry is a unique capability supporting a range of production microelectronic devices (Silicon, Gallium Arsenide, Gallium Nitride, Silicon Carbide and other semiconductor types) and providing leading edge technology development in Superconducting Electronics, Ultra-Wideband Electronics and other Beyond-Moore’s-Law technologies. Our devices support a broad range of Northrop Grumman ground-based, airborne, and space systems.

ATL’s multidisciplinary teams support the full semiconductor lifecycle, including design, mask making, wafer fabrication, test, and assembly. The organization operates at the intersection of advanced technology, production execution, and national security mission support.

Position Summary

The Director of ATL Wafer Fabrication will serve as a manager of managers
and lead a large, complex organization spanning key wafer fabrication functions, including:

Process Engineering
Process Integration Engineering
Equipment Engineering
Wafer Fab Operations

The Director will be responsible for leadership of resources, execution, and organizational performance across the wafer fabrication enterprise. The role includes responsibility for staffing, work prioritization, budget oversight, cross-functional alignment, and execution support for business and program objectives. Functional responsibilities include hiring, onboarding, performance management, time-charging approval, and employee development.

Leadership Opportunity

The successful candidate will be a strong semiconductor and manufacturing engineering leader with demonstrated experience improving safety, quality, delivery, and cost performance in a complex operating environment. This individual will bring leadership presence to guide a large organization through growth, transformation, and execution challenges while maintaining strong alignment with business priorities, customer commitments, and program needs.

This Role Requires a Leader Who Can

Lead through managers and build a high-performing leadership team
Establish clear operating rhythms and execution discipline
Integrate engineering, operations, and program stakeholders around common objectives
Make sound, data-informed decisions in a fast-paced, mission-driven environment
Foster a culture of accountability, innovation, inclusion, and continuous improvement

Technical credibility in semiconductor manufacturing and microelectronic process environments is important. At the same time, this role is intended for a leader who can direct, integrate, and elevate deep technical teams rather than personally serve as the expert in every process domain.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Business and a minimum of 10 years related leadership experience in semiconductor-related operations, manufacturing, engineering, closely related advanced manufacturing environments and/or program management
Demonstrated success leading managers and cross-functional teams in complex manufacturing environments, including large organizations operating in 24/7 settings
Proven ability to drive operational, organizational, and/or technology transformation while fostering an inclusive, high-engagement culture
Demonstrated leadership in improving safety, quality, delivery, and cost performance within a manufacturing environment
Experience operating in a defense, aerospace, national security, or other highly regulated manufacturing environment with mission-critical quality, delivery, and customer requirements
Experience partnering with program leadership to align manufacturing and engineering execution with cost, schedule, technical, and delivery commitments
Demonstrated ability to translate business priorities, customer commitments, and program requirements into operational plans, workforce priorities, and execution actions
Demonstrated critical thinking, sound judgment, and data-informed decision-making in a fast-paced and high-consequence environment
Strong business and financial acumen, with the ability to balance operational needs with broader enterprise and program objectives
Excellent verbal, written, and presentation skills, including the ability to communicate effectively with executive leadership, engineers, shop floor employees, and support functions
Ability to obtain and maintain a Top Secret clearance with SCI access
U.S. Citizenship required

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelors degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Business, or a related field with minimum of 15 years related leadership experience in semiconductor-related operations, manufacturing, engineering, closely related advanced manufacturing environments and/or program management
Experience supporting both semiconductor technology development and production/manufacturing operations
Experience across silicon and/or compound semiconductor technologies
Experience supporting defense industrial base programs across development, transition to production, and/or sustainment environments
Experience participating in customer reviews, program reviews, manufacturing readiness reviews, or recovery planning in support of government or defense customers
Experience working across program management, business management, supply chain, quality, and engineering to manage execution risk, delivery performance, and issue escalation
Familiarity with security, export control, compliance, and contractual requirements that influence defense manufacturing operations
Experience balancing technology development, production priorities, and customer commitments in support of defense or mission-driven programs
Experience with digital manufacturing, automation, data-driven operations, or Industry 4.0 initiatives
Active Top Secret clearance with SCI access

Primary Level Salary Range: $194,600.00 - $292,000.00

The above salary range represents a general guideline; however, Northrop Grumman considers a number of factors when determining base salary offers such as the scope and responsibilities of the position and the candidate's experience, education, skills and current market conditions.

Depending on the position, employees may be eligible for overtime, shift differential, and a discretionary bonus in addition to base pay. Annual bonuses are designed to reward individual contributions as well as allow employees to share in company results. Employees in Vice President or Director positions may be eligible for Long Term Incentives. In addition, Northrop Grumman provides a variety of benefits including health insurance coverage, life and disability insurance, savings plan, Company paid holidays and paid time off (PTO) for vacation and/or personal business.

The application period for the job is estimated to be 20 days from the job posting date. However, this timeline may be shortened or extended depending on business needs and the availability of qualified candidates.

For our complete EEO and pay transparency statement, please visit http://www.northropgrumman.com/EEO. U.S. Citizenship is required for all positions with a government clearance and certain other restricted positions.

added.title: Head of Engineering
added.description:
About Authorium

Authorium is a high-growth GovTech SaaS company transforming how government agencies manage administrative operations. Our platform replaces fragmented document management solutions and decades-old legacy systems with a unified user interaction and data layer that manages billions of dollars in public funds; serving state, local, and federal agencies that in turn support millions of citizens and businesses. Authorium sits at the intersection of modernization, public service, and technology innovation like AI-enabled workflows. Our team moves fast, collaborates across teams, and builds for impact.

About The Head Of Engineering Role

We are hiring a Head of Engineering to build and grow the team that builds the platform that state and local governments use to manage their complex workflows such as procurement, contract management, and grant management.

This senior engineering seat reports directly to the executive leadership. The Head of Engineering is a builder and a leader: owning the team, the technical execution, and executing with excellence on behalf of our customers. Authorium’s engineering team is small, but mighty and growing. We are looking for a leader that can get directly engaged in the work of the engineering team, directly execute key initiatives, and provide guidance and direction for the team.

You will work collaboratively across both on-shore and off-shore engineering squads to deliver a platform experience that is highly secure, meets some of the most stringent compliance requirements, and provides an excellent user experience to our customers and their stakeholders. Our customers are government agencies with real procurement deadlines, real compliance obligations, and limited tolerance for downtime. This is mission-critical software delivery and important work is tied to its reliability, performance, and experience.

What You'll Own

Hands-On Technical Contribution:
You are comfortable in the codebase. You are able to take work yourself rather vs. only routing it. You personally investigate complex, ambiguous problems before deciding how to tackle them with the team. You are a technical mentor to the engineering teams you work with.

Team Leadership:
Lead, coach, and grow a small blended team of full-time engineers, contractors, and an offshore agency partner across multiple time zones. Run 1:1s and career coaching, set clear expectations, manage capacity, and build a culture of collaboration and ownership and excitement around delivery.

Delivery Accountability:
Own what engineering commits to and whether it lands. Set priorities, unblock the team, set realistic dates, surface slippage before it becomes a customer conversation, and course-correct in the open. Delivery predictability is the metric that matters most in your first year.

Technical Execution & Architecture:
Own architecture and technical-debt decisions inside the platform and interface with security and compliance leaders. Create documented plans that acknowledge tradeoffs and guide executive decisionmaking. Be a critical member of the leadership team driving Authorium’s platform vision forward.

Engineering Quality:
Set the standard. Own code review norms, testing expectations, deployment safety, and the delivery and reliability metrics the team is measured against.

Production Reliability & Security:
Own uptime, incident response, and on-call structure. Partner with InfoSec and Compliance on the security and compliance posture our customers audit us against, including public-sector requirements as we expand.

AI-Native Engineering Practice:
Champion tools like Claude and Cursor across the team to remove toil and create leverage. Define where agents are trusted, where their output is reviewed, what quality bar applies to agent-produced code, and how we measure output.

Cross-Functional Partnership:
Work directly with Product, Delivery/Implementation, Customer Experience, and Solutions. Translate business priorities into scoped, sequenced engineering plans, and engineering constraints into language non-technical colleagues and government customers can act on. Expect to be in front of customers when it matters.

Hiring:
Interview, assess, and help set the technical bar for engineering hires. Plan, forecast, and manage team capacity.

What Success Looks Like

First 30 Days:
Learn the codebase and the customer business case — ship something real with support from the team. Get to know the architecture, the fragile parts, the open incidents, and every person on the team. You have a clear-eyed read on where delivery actually stands.

First 90 Days:
Delivery commitments are yours and they are being met and/or negotiated. The team's operating cadence — planning, review, on-call, incident response — is understood and running. Documented execution plans against capacity and priorities are the norm.

What We're Looking For

7+ years building software, with at least 2–3 years leading engineers directly — and you are still writing and reviewing code today
Strong fundamentals in distributed systems and cloud architecture
Demonstrable recent technical depth: you can walk us through an architecture you designed, a production incident you personally diagnosed, and a technical decision you got wrong and corrected
Track record of maintaining predictable quality and delivery, with specifics on how you managed it and what it cost
Experience leading a distributed team, holding quality and communication together across time zones
Fluency with modern AI-assisted development, plus a real point of view on where agent-generated code needs human scrutiny and where it does not
Comfortable in a growing startup environment where capacity and capabilities are being defined, refined, and operationalized.
Strong internal and external communication skills; written, calls, in-person engagements.

BONUS POINTS

Experience at an early-to-mid-stage startup
Experience in GovTech, public-sector SaaS, or another regulated, audited environment (FedRAMP, StateRAMP, SOC 2, HIPAA)
Experience building or scaling an offshore engineering function
Based in San Francisco Bay Area or Washington DC

What We Offer

Salary Range: $200,000–$250,000
Stock options (details at offer stage)
100% benefits coverage for employee
401K Profit Share plan
Flexible PTO
Home office stipend
Comprehensive wellness benefits
Commuter stipend for hybrid roles
Direct executive engagement, real proximity and support for company decision making
Genuine ownership of the platform's technical execution and the shape and direction of the team that builds it
Experience working for a mission-forward organization, operating as a public benefit corporation with a mission to support the critical work of government

Compensation Range: $200K - $250K

added.title: Director - Product Security
added.description:
About Us

Rivian and Volkswagen Group Technologies is a joint venture between two industry leaders with a clear vision for automotive’s next chapter. From operating systems to zonal controllers to cloud and connectivity solutions, we’re addressing the challenges of electric vehicles through technology that will set the standards for software-defined vehicles around the world.

The road to the future is uncharted. By combining our expertise across connectivity, AI, security and more, we’ll map a new way forward. Working together, we’ll create a future that’s more connected, more intelligent, more sustainable for everyone.

Role Summary

As the Director of Product Security, you will lead a structured, high-performing product security team at one of the most consequential software-defined vehicle platforms in the automotive industry. This is an engineering leadership role. You will work shoulder-to-shoulder with elite software and hardware engineers, driving technical excellence, elevating the people and practices already in place, and embedding security into the DNA of how we build. You own the execution, not just the vision, and you will be measured by the results your team delivers. Reporting to the Sr. Director, Systems Engineering, Safety and Software Quality, you will lead the end-to-end product security strategy for Rivian and Volkswagen Group Technologies’ joint platform, a technology stack that will underpin millions of future electric vehicles across Rivian, Volkswagen, Audi, Scout, and beyond.

This is not a compliance role. This is a builder’s role. You will embed security into the DNA of our zonal architecture, over-the-air update pipeline, cloud infrastructure, and autonomous driving stack. Working shoulder-to-shoulder with elite software and hardware engineers who share your obsession with getting it right. You’ll own the discipline, lead the team, and set the standard for what product security looks like at the intersection of Silicon Valley and the global automotive industry. he team and structure are in place. We are looking for a leader who inherits a high-performing org, develops the people within it, and evolves the team over time to meet the demands of an ever-changing security landscape, building on what's working while continuously raising the bar. This role is located in our Palo Alto, CA office and reports directly into the Sr. Director, Systems Engineering, Safety and Software Quality.

Responsibilities

Product Security Strategy & Architecture: Lead a team that will define and own the multi-year product security roadmap for Rivian and RV Tech’s joint SDV (Software Defined Vehicle) platform. Translate business objectives, threat landscapes, and regulatory requirements into a coherent, executable security strategy spanning vehicle firmware, cloud backend, mobile applications, and the OTA update pipeline.
Secure-by-Design Engineering: Embed security across the full software development lifecycle. Partner with software, hardware, and platform engineering teams to conduct threat modeling and TARA (Threat Analysis and Risk Assessment), development of security requirements for implementation, systematic test definition and execution on SIL (software-in-loop), HIL (hardware-in-loop) and test vehicle levels. You will also establish secure coding guidelines to be used across all core engineering teams and build automated security tooling (SAST, DAST, fuzzing) into CI/CD pipelines. Champion a “security by design” culture across a global engineering org of 1,500+.
Automotive & Connected Vehicle Security: Lead adhering to compliance and security engineering efforts for automotive cybersecurity standards including ISO/SAE 21434 and UN Regulation No. 155. Secure zonal and E/E architecture, ECU communication buses (CAN, Automotive Ethernet), telematics, V2X, and ADAS/autonomy stacks. Own security of OTA update signing and delivery infrastructure.
Vulnerability Management & Red Team Programs: Build and operate a world-class vulnerability management program covering vehicle software, cloud services, and mobile apps. Establish and manage a bug bounty program and coordinate penetration testing across all product surfaces. Oversee triage, prioritization, and remediation tracking in partnership with engineering teams.
Supply Chain & Third-Party Security: Define and enforce security requirements across Tier-1 and Tier-2 automotive suppliers and software vendors. Build Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) practices, oversee third-party security assessments, and ensure supply chain integrity across the full software stack shared between Rivian and Volkswagen Group brands.
AI & Autonomy Security: Secure RV Tech’s AI and autonomy platform, including the Rivian Unified Intelligence stack and in-vehicle AI systems. Develop threat models for ML pipelines, model integrity, adversarial input attacks, and in-vehicle inference security. Stay at the forefront of AI security as a rapidly evolving attack surface in safety-critical systems.
Incident Response & PSIRT: Build and lead the Product Security Incident Response Team (PSIRT) for RV Tech. Establish coordinated disclosure processes, incident playbooks, and executive communication frameworks. Ensure rapid and effective response to security incidents affecting vehicle or platform software.
Team Leadership & Talent Development: Inspire a high-performance product security team across Palo Alto, Irvine, Vancouver and Berlin. Create a culture of ownership, technical excellence, and continuous improvement while fostering collaboration across the RV Tech core engineering team and parent companies.
Executive & Cross-Organizational Leadership: Report directly to the Sr. Director, Product Security, Safety and Software Quality and present to executive leadership and the board on product security posture, program maturity, and key risks. Engage with industry forums and standards bodies (Auto-ISAC, NHTSA, UNECE WP.29) as needed to stay current on the evolving regulatory and threat landscape.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications:

12+ years of progressive experience in cybersecurity, with at least 5 years in product security leadership at a software-defined product company (automotive, consumer electronics, aerospace, robotics, or similar).
Deep technical expertise in application security, embedded systems security, or automotive cybersecurity with a hands-on engineering background, not purely managerial.
Demonstrated experience leading and upleveling an inherited product security or AppSec team, developing people, elevating practices, and driving execution within an existing org structure. Greenfield build experience is a plus but not the primary requirement for this role.
Proven ability to influence and drive security posture across engineering organizations without direct authority - the credibility to be taken seriously in a room full of elite engineers.
Strong working knowledge of threat modeling methodologies (eg STRIDE, PASTA, TARA), secure SDLC practices, and vulnerability management programs including coordinated disclosure.
Experience securing cloud-native architectures at scale (GCP, AWS, or Azure) including cloud-to-vehicle communication channels and data pipelines.
Track record of operating at the executive level presenting to the board, partnering with the C-suite, and translating deeply technical risk into business-level language.
B.S. or M.S. in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or equivalent practical experience.

Experience at a mission-driven, high-velocity technology company

added.description:
We Are:

Accenture is a leading global professional services company that helps the world’s leading businesses, governments and other organizations build their digital core, optimize their operations, accelerate revenue growth, and enhance citizen services—creating tangible value at speed and scale. We are a talent- and innovation-led company with approximately 774,000 people serving clients in more than 120 countries. Technology is at the core of change today, and we are one of the world’s leaders in helping drive that change, with strong ecosystem relationships. We combine our strength in technology and leadership in cloud, AI and data with unmatched industry experience, functional expertise, and global delivery capability. We are uniquely able to deliver tangible outcomes because of our broad range of services, solutions and assets across Consulting, Strategy, Technology, Operations, Industry X and Song. These capabilities, together with our culture of shared success and commitment to creating 360° value, enable us to help our clients reinvent and build trusted, lasting relationships. We measure our success by the 360° value we create for our clients, each other, our shareholders, partners, and communities. Visit us at accenture.com.

In Technology, we work with the world’s leading organizations to build and manage the digital and AI-enabled foundations that power reinvention. Our Managed Reinvention Services (MRS) practice is rewriting the playbook on managed services—shifting clients from traditional, labor-led application management toward an AI-first, agentic operating model that reshapes tech economics and delivers measurable business outcomes at speed and scale.

You Are:

Our MRS Senior Managers are accountable owners—not coordinators. We need leaders who can run complex, multi-tower managed services accounts end-to-end, shape the agentic operating model that replaces traditional AMS delivery, and build the client relationships that turn a run contract into a long-term reinvention partnership. This is not a generalist role. You will be expected to engage CIOs and technology executives with credibility, drive compounding delivery value, and actively contribute to the growth of Accenture’s MRS business.

The Work:

As a Technology Delivery Senior Manager—Managed Reinvention Services, you will:

Own end-to-end delivery accountability — hold full P&L and outcome responsibility across multi-tower managed services accounts spanning AMS, IMS, Security, and Data & AI, driving toward committed business and technology results.

Architect and operationalize AI-first delivery models — design and implement agentic operations frameworks using Accenture’s Reinvention.AI platform and GenWizard capabilities, progressing clients deliberately along the autonomy maturity curve from human-augmented (L2) toward full autonomous operations (L4/L5).

Reshape tech economics — shift client Run spend toward Reinvention capital by systematically driving cost takeout, technical debt reduction, and throughput gains—converting efficiency savings into funded transformation.

Lead the workforce transition to agentic operations — build and evolve delivery teams composed of AI agent fleets and human SREs, define new role frameworks for the agentic era, and establish the governance and escalation model for autonomous operations.

Build and expand senior client relationships — serve as the primary technology advisor to CIOs and senior IT leadership, translating delivery performance into reinvention value and expanding the engagement scope over time.

Drive continuous modernization within the run model — embed architecture simplification, platform modernization, and resilience engineering as standing deliverables within managed services—not as separate projects.

Shape and win MRS pursuits — bring delivery credibility and operating model depth to competitive bids, contributing to solution design, commercial structuring, and MRS value proposition development across the portfolio.

Travel may be required for this role. The amount of travel will vary from 0 to 100% depending on business need and client requirement

Here’s What You Need:

Minimum of 8 years of technology delivery experience, including direct P&L ownership of large-scale application and/or infrastructure managed services accounts across complex, multi-tower environments

Minimum of 3 years of hands-on experience designing or operating AI-driven delivery models — including AIOps, agentic automation, GenAI-powered ITSM, or intelligent observability in production managed services contexts

Minimum of 8 years of demonstrated accountability for multi-tower delivery across three or more of the following: AMS, IMS, Security Operations, Data & AI, Cloud Engineering

Minimum of 8 years of Demonstrable experience with one or more of the following:

Designing and governing agentic or autonomous operations models (fleet orchestration, SRE frameworks, L1–L5 autonomy progression)

Outcome-based or autonomy-based commercial constructs (XLAs, shared savings, value-linked pricing)

Platform engineering, self-healing infrastructure, or AI-powered SDLC at enterprise scale

FinOps, tech value management, or run-to-reinvention capital reallocation

Minimum of 5 years of proven track record engaging CIOs, CTOs, and C-1 technology leaders on managed services strategy, operating model evolution, and transformation roadmaps

Minimum of 5 years of Industry ( CNR) and manufacturing expertise

Bachelor's degree or equivalent (minimum 12 years' work experience). If Associate’s Degree, must have equivalent minimum 6-year work experience

Bonus points if:

You have a Master’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, Business, or a related field

You have familiarity with Accenture’s Reinvention.AI platform, GenWizard, or comparable AI-native managed services platforms (e.g., ServiceNow AI, Dynatrace, PagerDuty AIOps)

You have Industry experience in Resources e.g., Energy, Utilities, Chemicals, or other asset-intensive sectors where tech economics transformation is a strategic CIO priority

You have experience shaping or contributing to large managed services pursuits, including RFP responses, operating model design, and commercial negotiations

You have strong command of managed services commercial constructs — T&M, fixed price, outcome-based, and autonomy-based pricing models; experience structuring and re-baselining contracts
